title: Senior Revenue Systems Specialist
description:
Greenhouse is the first Orchestrated Hiring Ecosystem: a single place that brings the right person and the right role together at the right time. Our [mission](https://www.greenhouse.com/mission) is to make hiring work for everyone – so we go to great lengths to hire great people because we believe that they’re the foundation of our success. At Greenhouse, you’ll join a team that collaborates purposefully, fosters inclusivity, and communicates with transparency and accountability so we can achieve our mission.

Join us to do the best work of your career, solving meaningful problems with remarkable teams.

Greenhouse is looking for a Senior Revenue Systems Specialist to join our team!

Revenue Systems owns the go-to-market technology stack at Greenhouse, from first outreach through renewal. As a Senior Revenue Systems Specialist, you’ll own systems work across both pre-sale and post-sale: Salesforce, our sales system of record, and the platforms our Customer Success and Customer Marketing teams work from every day, currently Gainsight and Accord. Breadth is a key aspect of this role, and you’ll have real latitude to shape where the stack goes next.

#### **Who will love this job**

- **A systems generalist** - you enjoy working across a stack rather than being confined to one corner of it, and you’re comfortable moving to where the work is
- **A solutions-oriented** **partner**- you can hear what the business is trying to accomplish and turn it into something that works, and you stay with a problem until the desired outcome is achieved
- **A curious builder** - you want to understand why a process exists before you automate it, and you’re comfortable saying when something doesn’t seem to make sense, including to the people asking for it
- **An owner** - you take a project from first conversation through rollout and adoption without needing it project-managed for you
- **An AI-fluent operator** - you already use tools like Claude, Glean, or ChatGPT in your day to day, and you’re interested in what they can do inside a revenue stack

#### **What you’ll do**

- Own and build solutions in Salesforce, including data model design, declarative automation, validation, permissions, page layouts, and reporting, taking projects from scoping and intake through rollout, adoption, and documentation
- Administer our post-sale platforms, including Gainsight and Accord, alongside our Customer Success Operations team, covering the rules engine, journey and email programs, surveys including NPS, and the workflows behind customer health scoring, CSM assignment, and account transfers
- Own integrations between Salesforce, Gainsight, and the rest of the stack, standing up new ones independently and eliminating the recurring failures that come with the existing ones
- Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Customer Marketing on their requests, working out whether the fix belongs in a system or somewhere else, and seeing it through to a working solution either way
- Lead platform migration and consolidation work as our tech stack changes, from evaluation and vendor assessment through data movement, cutover, and adoption
- Hold a point of view on where the stack should go, surfacing the opportunities and the risks in our implementation rather than waiting to be asked
- Document what you build, and bring request volume down over time through automation and self-service
- Additional projects and responsibilities as business needs require

#### **You should have**

- Several years in revenue operations, customer success operations, business systems, or platform administration.
- B2B SaaS experience.
- Deep hands-on Salesforce administration experience: data model design, declarative automation, permissions and sharing, reporting, and the judgment to know when not to build. You should be comfortable making medium to large changes to a production org and reasoning about the performance and scale implications of your configuration choices.
- Hands-on ownership of Gainsight or a comparable post-sale platform (e.g., Totango, ChurnZero, Planhat), with enough depth to configure independently and to hold a credible view on whether the platform is serving the business.
- Experience standing up integrations without support, and a record of eliminating recurring failures rather than only resolving them.
- Experience owning a platform migration or consolidation end to end, including the data movement.
- A track record of taking a problem from the first report through to a working solution.
- Comfort operating as the most knowledgeable person in the room on a platform, and the instinct to bring others along rather than becoming the only one who can do the work.
- Clear writing. A real part of this job is explaining to a non-technical stakeholder what you built and how to use it, or what went wrong and what you did about it.
- Experience across more than one post-sale platform is a plus. So is exposure to Salesforce CPQ, enrichment tooling like Clay, or building with MCP and agentic tooling against enterprise systems.
- Your own unique talents! Your background has given you a unique perspective and set of transferable skills that aren’t always in alignment with a given role, but those are qualities we value at Greenhouse. If you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications outlined above, we still strongly encourage you to apply.

_Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis._

_If you are based in California, we encourage you to read this important information for California residents linked_ [_here_](https://www.greenhouse.io/ccpa-candidate) _._

_The national pay range for this role is $88,100.00 - $127,700.00. Individual compensation will be commensurate with the candidate's experience and qualifications. Certain roles may be eligible for additional compensation, including stock option awards, bonuses, and merit increases. Additionally, certain roles have the opportunity to receive sales commissions that are based on the terms of the sales commission plan applicable to the role._

Greenhouse provides a variety of benefits to employees, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, basic life insurance, mental health resources, financial wellness benefits, and a fully paid parental leave program. For US-based employees, we offer short-term and long-term disability coverage, a 401(k) plan and company match. U.S. based employees also receive, per calendar year, up to 14 scheduled paid holidays and up to 80 hours of paid sick leave. Non-exempt employees accrue up to 20-25 days of paid vacation time annually, depending on tenure, and exempt employees have flexible paid time off (PTO).

The anticipated closing date for this role is Friday, November 13, 2026 **.**

description:
#### Company Description

Ubisoft is a global leader in the video game industry, with teams around the world creating original and memorable experiences, from Assassin's Creed and Rainbow Six to Just Dance and much more. We are convinced that diversity of perspectives allows players and teams alike to thrive. If you are passionate about innovation and pushing the boundaries of entertainment, join us and help create the unknown!

#### Job Description

As a **3D programmer** at Ubisoft Montreal, you will focus on the rendering systems of the **Assassin's Creed HEXE project**. You will work closely with the **Anvil Pipeline rendering team** to maintain the stability, efficiency and adaptability of the engine on current-generation consoles and on personal computers.

**What you will do**

- **Contribute** to the entire rendering engine, including opaque rendering, shadows, post-processing effects and compute-based systems
- **Support** rendering in close collaboration with the Anvil Pipeline rendering team
- **Diagnose** project-specific issues, including GPU stalls and complex rendering bugs
- **Evaluate performance** and implement optimizations across the entire rendering pipeline
- **Design and implement** alternative rendering solutions adapted to consoles with more limited capabilities
- **Support** the Toolmode Data Generation pipeline from a rendering perspective

#### Qualifications

**What you bring to the team**

- A bachelor's degree in computer science, computer engineering or equivalent.
- **Mastery of modern real-time rendering systems**, including opaque rendering, shadows, post-processing effects and compute-based processing pipelines
- **Practical experience** shipping games on **PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S** or **Nintendo Switch 2**
- **Solving platform-specific rendering issues**, including GPU stalls
- **Using GPU profiling tools** to identify and fix performance issues
- **Navigating a large codebase** and contributing effectively to less familiar systems
- **Ideally, experience with proprietary game engines**, such as Anvil
- **Ideally, familiarity with tool and data generation pipelines**, such as Toolmode
- **Ideally, experience collaborating with engine or production pipeline teams spread across multiple studios**

**What to send us**

- Your resume highlighting your skills
- Code samples, links to your repositories or relevant projects

title: Quality Control Analyst (85389)
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

Serves as an adjunct to the Technical Director and Quality Manager to assure customer claims are reviewed, documented, and processed in a timely manner. Also, responsible for maintaining and updating all the associated Quality Department databases and serves as a back- up for Incoming Quality Tech.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  1. Input new claims in Product Concerns and Returns database.
  2. Inspect submitted samples of defective film in conjunction with Quality Eng.
  3. Review and report on inventory of suspect film based on claim
  4. Communicate findings with Quality Manager/Sales/Production as necessary
  5. Compute costing of claims
  6. Maintain Tolerance/Cert Databases
  7. Input all incoming C of As into system

ADDITIONAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  1. Create and post Quality Alerts as required.
  2. Attend weekly Claims Meetings for status reporting
  3. Attend daily Production Meeting
  4. Attend weekly MRB Meeting
  5. Assist Incoming Quality Tech with duties as needed
  6. Investigates product quality problems using 8D methods, determines root cause, gathers and analyzes data and implements corrective action to reduce or eliminate cause.
  7. Perform a root cause analysis using statistical methods (e.g., design of experiment (DOE), DMAIC, 8D, and other problem solving tools. Performs Process Capability Analysis (Cpk), GR&R, and other statistical techniques aimed at reducing variance and improving yields. Interacts with representatives from a variety of functional groups, including design, manufacturing, engineering,
  8. purchasing, production and inspection, personnel, and customer and supplier representatives on quality issues.
  9. Performs all work in a manner providing safety and health of self and other plant personnel.
  10. Supports manufacturing by troubleshooting issues that either cause or potentially cause work stoppages and reduced throughput times.
  11. Implements corrective action to reduce or eliminate cause.
  12. Promotes the use of Lean and Six Sigma tools
  13. Promotes a safe work environment.
  14. Uses 5S techniques in the workplace/area.

MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS (QMS/EMS) RESPONSIBILITIES:

  1. Improves work processes.
  2. Provides input and verifies that documented procedures are adequate and accurate and in support of achievement of
  3. the strategy
  4. Understands the IMS policy and how it applies.
  5. Keeps records and data on pertinent business outcomes.
  6. Participates in internal audits.
  7. Participates in ongoing process improvement.
  8. Participates in external registration and surveillance audits.
  9. Directly supports methods and practices of the IMS Process through personal compliance and visible support actions.
  10. Supports CSR activities

QUALITY SYSTEMS RESPONSIBILITIES:

Responsible for following all ISO processes and procedures

DESIRED MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  1. Bachelor’s degree in a Technical Discipline, specifically, Polymer Chemistry, Plastics or Materials.
  2. Specific certifications and experience may substitute for degree.
  3. Statistical process control techniques and assessment experience.
  4. Root Cause Analysis, Corrective Action and Improvement Plan experience.

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS:

TOOLS AND EQUIPMENT USED:

  1. Advanced skills in Microsoft Office Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Access.
  2. Experience with ISO.
  3. Experience with quality improvement techniques, technical audit and corrective/preventative action is desired.
  4. Six Sigma and Lean Manufacturing experience desired.
  5. Experience in a web handling environment (roll-to-roll) preferred.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit or stand as needed. May require walking primarily on a level surface for periodic periods during the day. Also, reaching above shoulder heights, below the waist or lifting as required to move materials throughout the workday. Proper lifting techniques required. Working conditions are normal for a laboratory and a manufacturing environment. While performing duties of this position, the employee must take the appropriate safety precautions and/or don the appropriate safety PPE when working in areas that may contain fumes, airborne particles, ultra violet radiation, toxic or caustic chemicals, etc. The employee may be occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts. This position may require occasional weekend and/or evening work. Occasional travel may also be required.

The performance of this position requires exposure to the manufacturing areas which require the use of personal protective equipment such as safety glasses and steel toe or composite toe shoes.

title: Senior Manager, Brand Voice & Creative
description:
Senior Manager, Global Brand Voice & Creative

Location: Lake Mary, FL (Hybrid)
Department: Brand & Digital Growth
Position Type: Full-Time, Exempt

About The IIA

The Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) is the global leader and recognized authority for the internal audit profession. We advance the profession worldwide through education, advocacy, certifications, standards, and professional resources.

Guided by our values of People First, Integrity, Collaboration, Accountability, and Innovation, we offer a collaborative, purpose-driven workplace where employees can grow professionally while making a global impact.

Why Join The IIA?

Join a global, mission-driven organization and help shape how The IIA communicates with members, customers, and internal audit professionals worldwide. You'll have the opportunity to influence global brand strategy, lead creative initiatives, and develop compelling content that strengthens audience engagement and drives organizational growth.

Position Summary

The IIA is seeking a highly skilled Senior Manager, Global Brand Voice & Creative to lead the development and execution of our global brand voice, messaging strategy, and creative content across digital and traditional marketing channels.

This is a hands-on leadership opportunity for an exceptional writer, storyteller, and creative strategist who can establish brand voice standards while personally developing high-impact copy for marketing campaigns, websites, email communications, and digital experiences.

The ideal candidate brings extensive experience in brand storytelling, copywriting, demand generation, lifecycle marketing, and creative team leadership, with the ability to translate complex concepts into clear, engaging, and conversion-focused messaging.

What You'll Do

Brand Voice, Messaging & Content Strategy

  • Develop and maintain The IIA's global brand voice, messaging architecture, editorial guidelines, and tone-of-voice standards.

  • Write, edit, and oversee high-impact content, including brand narratives, marketing campaigns, executive communications, website copy, and digital experiences.

  • Translate complex professional and technical information into clear, compelling, audience-focused messaging.

  • Establish brand voice guidelines, templates, and training to ensure consistent communication across teams and external partners.

  • Provide creative and editorial direction for major brand and marketing initiatives.

Demand Generation & Lifecycle Marketing

  • Lead messaging and copy development across the customer journey, including awareness, acquisition, lead nurturing, conversion, onboarding, retention, and advocacy.

  • Develop personalized email campaigns, automated nurture journeys, landing pages, lead-generation content, and account-based marketing (ABM) communications.

  • Partner with Marketing, Digital, Membership, Learning, Certification, and Sales teams to align messaging with audience needs and business objectives.

  • Apply UX writing and content design principles to improve website experiences, customer journeys, and conversion opportunities.

  • Use audience insights, campaign analytics, and testing to optimize messaging and engagement.

Digital Marketing & Creative Campaigns

  • Guide brand voice and content across social media, paid advertising, websites, email, search, video, and integrated marketing campaigns.

  • Develop creative concepts, messaging frameworks, campaign briefs, and calls to action that support engagement and conversion.

  • Ensure content reflects brand standards, accessibility best practices, SEO principles, and audience expectations.

  • Collaborate with channel owners to evaluate content performance and improve campaign effectiveness.

Creative Leadership & Brand Governance

  • Lead, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary creative team, including writers, designers, and production professionals.

  • Manage agency and freelance partnerships, creative workflows, content reviews, and project priorities.

  • Establish quality standards and processes that support efficient, consistent creative execution.

  • Partner with senior leadership to strengthen brand positioning, creative strategy, and messaging effectiveness.

  • Present creative recommendations, brand initiatives, and performance insights to executive stakeholders.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, English, Journalism, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

  • 8+ years of progressive experience in copywriting, brand voice, editorial direction, content design, or creative leadership, with significant hands-on writing responsibilities.

  • A strong portfolio demonstrating original writing, brand storytelling, digital marketing content, UX writing, and demand-generation campaigns.

  • Proven experience developing and managing brand voice guidelines, messaging frameworks, and editorial standards.

  • Hands-on experience creating lifecycle marketing campaigns, personalized email journeys, lead-generation content, landing pages, nurture campaigns, and account-based marketing communications.

  • Experience developing content across websites, social media, paid digital advertising, email, search, video, and integrated marketing channels.

  • Strong understanding of audience segmentation, customer journeys, conversion optimization, content testing, and marketing performance.

  • Exceptional writing, editing, communication, storytelling, and presentation skills.

  • Experience leading multidisciplinary creative teams and managing agency or freelance partners.

  • Strong project management, stakeholder collaboration, and organizational skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with professional associations, membership organizations, credentialing bodies, professional education, or global mission-driven brands.

  • Experience supporting rebranding, brand modernization, or digital transformation initiatives.

  • Familiarity with CRM, marketing automation, CMS, personalization, and analytics platforms such as Marketo, HubSpot, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, or comparable tools.

  • Knowledge of UX writing, content design, SEO, accessibility, audience research, and omnichannel marketing.

  • Experience developing messaging for global audiences while maintaining consistent brand standards.

Equal Opportunity Employer

The Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all employees are treated with dignity and respect. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

title: Engineering - Team Leader
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

Respond and attend to guest repair requests. Communicate with guests/customers to resolve maintenance issues. Perform preventive maintenance on tools and equipment, including cleaning and lubrication. Visually inspect tools, equipment, or machines. Carry equipment (e.g., tools, radio). Identify, locate, and operate all shut-off valves for equipment and utility shut-offs for buildings. Maintain maintenance inventory and requisition parts and supplies as needed. Assure each day’s activities and problems that occur are communicated to the other shifts using approved communication programs and standards. Display thorough knowledge of building systems, emergency response, and building documentation including reading standard blue prints and electrical schematics concerning plumbing and HVAC. Display advanced engineering operations skills and general mechanical ability. Display professional journeyman level expertise in at least three of the following areas with basic skills in the remaining: air conditioning and refrigeration, electrical, plumbing, carpentry and finish skills, mechanical, general building management, pneumatic/electronic systems and controls, and/or energy conservation. Display solid knowledge and skill in the safe use of hand and power tools and other materials required to perform repair and maintenance tasks. Safely perform highly complex repairs of the physical property, electrical, plumbing and mechanical equipment, air conditioners, refrigeration and pool heaters - ensuring all methods, materials and practices meet company standards and Local and National codes - with little or no supervision. Perform routine inspections of the entire property, noting safety hazards, lack of illumination, down equipment (such as ice makers, fans, extractors, pumps), and take immediate corrective action. Inspect and repair all mechanical equipment including, but not limited to: appliances, HVAC, electrical and plumbing components, diagnose and repair of boilers, pumps and related components. Use the Lockout/Tagout system before performing any maintenance work. Display thorough knowledge of maintenance contracts and vendors. Display advanced knowledge of engineering computer programs related to preventative maintenance, energy management, and other systems, including devices that interact with such programs. Perform advanced troubleshooting of hotel Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) systems. Display the ability to train and mentor other engineers (e.g., Engineers I, II, and III) as necessary and supervise work in progress and act in a supervisory role in the absence of supervisors and/or management. Display ability to perform Engineer on Duty responsibilities, including readings and rounds.

title: AP Specialist
description:
SUMMARY

The primary purpose of this position is to perform crucial job duties that ensure vendors get paid for services and products rendered. The Accounts Payable Specialist provides both administrative and financial support by processing, verifying and reconciling Invoices. The incumbent monitors accounts payable (AP) to confirm all recurring bills are received a entered in the correct period and company. Advantix maintains approximately 45 separate payable entities and each invoice must be charged to the correct entity and general ledger (GL) accounts. The incumbent monitors workflow and period cut off procedures. Reconciliation of irregularities is required.

All activities must support Advantix’s strategic goals and objectives and produce results that accomplish the goals of the overall organization.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

Primary areas of responsibility and tasks that may typically be expected include but are not limited to:

Accounts Payable

  • Manages accounts payable using accounting software and other programs.
  • Reconciles vendor statements to in house recorded.
  • Handles accounts payable for separate entities and vendors.
  • Tracks and reconciles intercompany transactions.
  • Analyzes workflow processes.
  • Establishes and maintains relationships with new and existing vendors.
  • Ensures bills are paid in a timely and accurate manner while adhering to departmental procedures.
  • Processes due invoices for payments.
  • Processes transactions and performing accounting duties such as account maintenance, recording entries and reconciling vendor accounts.
  • Sorts payables into batches and complete data entry daily.
  • Provides printed checks to appropriate directors for signatures.
  • Mails authorized checks or distributes checks with necessary attachments.
  • Files copies of authorized checks with appropriate invoices.
  • Maintains responsibility for assisting in Tenant accounting and bank reconciliations as needed.
  • Maintains responsibility for additional check processing requirements as needed.
  • Maintains filing up to date for review purposes.

Annual 1099 Reporting

  • Reconciles reporting files with historical records.
  • Identifies and corrects 1099 vendor information.
  • Prepares electronic 1099 reporting file for submission to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS).
  • Submits 1099 and 1096 forms in a timely manner.
  • Maintains and updates W-9 and insurance documentation.
  • Manages State and Federal Grants including grant job costing, budgeting and analysis
  • Performs other related duties as assigned and/or required.

BEHAVIORAL COMPETENCIES

Problem Solving: Identifies and resolves problems in a timely manner; gathers and analyzes information skillfully; develops alternative solutions; works well in group problem solving situations; uses reason even when dealing with sensitive topics and/or irate customers.

Job Knowledge: Exhibits requisite knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the position effectively. Demonstrates knowledge of policies, procedures, goals, objectives, operational entities, requirements, and activities as they apply to the assigned organizational entity. Uses appropriate judgment & decision making in accordance with level of responsibility.

Customer Service: Understands that all employees have external and/or internal customers that they provide services and information to; honors all the organization’s commitments to customers/residents by providing helpful, courteous, accessible, responsive and knowledgeable customer service.

Interpersonal Skills: Focuses on solving conflict, not blaming; maintains confidentiality; listens to others without interrupting; establishes rapport when working with others.

Teamwork: Cooperates with others to accomplish common goals; works with employees within and across his/her department to achieve shared goals; treats others with dignity and respect and maintains friendly demeanor; values the contributions of others.

Results Orientation: Consistently delivers required agency results; sets and achieves achievable, consistently complies with quality standards and meets deadlines; maintains focus on organizational goals.

Accountability: Accepts full responsibility for self and contribution as a team member; displays honesty and truthfulness; confronts problems quickly; displays a strong commitment to organizational success and inspires others to commit to goals; demonstrates a commitment to delivering on his/her public duty and presenting oneself as a credible representative of the organization to maintain the public’s trust.

Professionalism: Approaches others in a tactful manner; reacts well under pressure; treats others with respect and consideration regardless of their status or position; accepts responsibility for own actions.

title: OCRP Residential Case Manager (4949)
description:
Here at Community House Mental Health Agency, we strive to provide a supportive family atmosphere in Seattle and King County for people with severe and persistent mental illness. Each person who walks through our door has a unique story, and we believe that everyone deserves to feel welcomed and valued.

The Diversion Residential Case Manager works as part of a team to provide behavioral health services, skills training, and community support in a residential setting within their assigned diversion program. This position is responsible for providing treatment and care coordination based on resident needs and the treatment plan, progress notes, and collaborative reviews for the assigned caseload, as well as support to all residents served as part of the care team.

At Community House, we value a strong work-life balance and aim to provide the best support for our workers. As a CHMHA employee, you will have access to a range of unique benefits, such as company-paid medical/dental/vision/disability insurance, a 403B retirement plan with employer match, continuing education credit, a personal unlimited Orca Card, and an employee assistance program with financial, mental, and legal assistance.

This position is located in Seattle, WA 98125.

SCHEDULE

Tuesday-Saturday, 8:00am-4:00pm

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Serve as secondary Case Manager and primary on-site contact for residents at assigned location, including advocating for and coordinating resident needs and services; assisting with Service Plans, Crisis Plans, and other documentation and providing consistent contacts, skills training, and care coordination to work towards goals
  • Coordinate with relevant internal and external departments to coordinate resident referrals, ensure timely intake into program, and review of individualized plans
  • Collaborate with care team to ensure all residents access needed treatment, support, case management, and appointments, including transportation to external providers
  • Ensure all interactions represent the five principles of trauma-informed care, including safety, choice, trustworthiness, collaboration, and empowerment
  • Coordinate access to medications for all clients through trained staff ensuring the seven rights of medication use are followed: right person, right medication, right time, right dose, right route, right reason (including refusal), and right documentation according to agency provided medication training
  • Actively participate in Shift Change meetings and complete associated documentation
  • Complete daily documentation in electronic medical record on resident interactions, medications dispensed when assigned, and other required documentation, ensuring an interaction or observation and subsequent documentation are completed for all residents across the team
  • Practice good financial stewardship of agency and contract resources, including how time is being spent, supplies are used, property is being maintained, etc.
  • Monitor spending of Petty Cash and other agency money to ensure accountability and appropriate use
  • Meet identified key performance indicators and metrics for the position as identified for the program, division, and agency
  • Participate in discharge planning and written summaries of treatment as needed for resident referral and releases of information
  • Assist with and support on-site cleaning, including skills training with residents to maintain personal and community spaces, laundry, and preparation for regular pest treatments
  • Provide immediate crisis intervention and resolution as needed
  • Always maintain resident and staff confidentiality

The Diversion Residential Case Manager works with care team to ensure high standards of care are provided within the program, including but not limited to:

  • Providing appropriate levels of treatment, skills training, and assistance are provided to residents in managing mental health symptoms and developing skills and insight to manage symptoms, including Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs) per their service plan and individual needs, such as assistance in hygiene needs, cleaning, finances, transportation, etc.
  • Partnering as a team to deliver current programming and fill vacant position duties
  • Working collaboratively with larger outpatient team of providers to support resident in actively working towards treatment goals
  • Coordinating care, such as scheduling, attending, and/or arranging transportation for appointments and other case management needs
  • Maintaining and documenting in resident charts and program trackers following agency, county, state, and federal guidelines.
  • Providing and receiving input as part of resident’s care team on service plan and progress, and collaborating with other providers such as primary care provider, housing staff for entering/maintaining/exiting housing, etc.
  • Facilitating regular group and individual activities, encounters, and specialized resident events, such as outings and holiday gatherings
  • Performing other duties as assigned.

title: Software Developer
description:
We are seeking a highly motivated Software Developer to join the Centre for Cancer Genetic Epidemiology (CCGE), within the Department of Public Health and Primary Care at the University of Cambridge.

CCGE is a world-leading research centre focused on understanding cancer susceptibility and aetiology through the analysis of large-scale genomic, epidemiological and healthcare data. Working with national and international collaborators, we develop innovative data-driven approaches to advance cancer prevention, early detection and risk-stratified healthcare.

This role offers the opportunity to develop software that supports cancer research and translates research findings into tools for clinical practice.

You will design, develop and maintain software across CCGE's research and clinical-translation portfolio, taking responsibility for defined components and projects. Working closely with the Senior Software Developer and multidisciplinary and multi-institutional colleagues, you will contribute across the software development lifecycle, from requirements gathering and prototyping to testing, deployment and ongoing support.

Alongside software development, you will lead the scoping, coordination and delivery of technology and service-improvement projects across the Centre. This will include engaging external suppliers, evaluating potential solutions and providing concise updates and recommendations to support decisions. You will work autonomously within agreed priorities, using initiative to move projects forward.

**Key responsibilities**

- Design, develop and maintain front-end web interfaces, back-end web servers and APIs.

- Gather stakeholder requirements and investigate, prototype and evaluate solutions.

- Maintain and deploy web applications, write tests and produce clear technical documentation.

- Co-lead user support and contribute to quality and regulatory-compliance activities for relevant software products.

- Evaluate emerging technologies and contribute advice on software roadmaps and technical direction.

- Coordinate technology and service-improvement projects, including work beyond software development.


**Applications should have**

- A degree in an appropriate subject, or equivalent knowledge, skills and understanding gained through experience and professional qualifications.

- Strong software engineering skills, including Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, web frameworks, databases, version control and automated testing. You will have experience contributing across the software development lifecycle, working with existing codebases and producing clear documentation.

- Strong organisational skills and a proactive approach, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively.

title: Research Associate in 2D (opto)spintronics and (spin)caloritronics
description:
Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for 12 months in the first instance.

We are looking for a Research Associate in 2D (opto)spintronics and (spin)caloritronics. Applicants should have significant experimental expertise in working with 2D materials and van der Waals heterostructures, particularly with electrical, spintronic, thermal and thermoelectric measurements in devices based on them.

The role holder will, together with a team of PhD students, design and carry out experimental investigations in the spintronic, orbitronics, thermal and thermoelectric properties of 2D materials and heterostructures, particularly including topological materials (e.g. Chern insulators and Weyl semimetals), magnets and ferroelectrics. They will perform device fabrication and characterisation using the facilities of the Guimarães group, CORDE, and the Cambridge Graphene Centre.

Applicants should hold (or be close to completing) a PhD in physics or a related field. Appointment at Research Associate is dependent on having a PhD. Those who have submitted but not yet received their PhD will initially be appointed at Research Assistant level and progress to Research Associate once the PhD is awarded.

title: Academic Advisor, Graduate Programs
description:
## Department

INDIANA UNIVERSITY ONLINE (UA-OEC-IUBLA)

## Department Information

[Indiana University (IU) Online](https://online.iu.edu/index.html) is dedicated to maintaining the academic integrity of an IU degree while expanding online education offerings to students locally, nationally, and internationally. As a university-wide office, IU Online provides strategic leadership in delivering online education, leveraging IU's scale, resources, and reputation. In alignment with the [IU 2030 Strategic Plan](https://strategicplan.iu.edu/index.html), IU Online advances student access and success through innovative online programs and services developed in collaboration with IU campuses.

IU Online, under the Office of the [Vice President for Student Success (VPSS)](https://vpsseie.iu.edu/index.html) , partners with IU's academic units, as well as University Information Technology Services (UITS)' Teaching and Learning Technologies (TLT) for instructional design and learning technology and with University Communications and Marketing (UCM) for marketing, to develop, launch, and maintain online programs. As of Fall 2026, IU Online offers nearly 200 academic programs, 50 of which are collaborative academic programs across IU's 9 campuses with an enrollment of 11,063 students. The office manages admissions, recruitment, student services, administration, advising, reporting, program and assessment support, and compliance for online programs.

## Job Summary

Department-Specific Responsibilities

- Reports to the Associate Director for Online Graduate Support.
- Provides academic advising and support for students pursuing or considering degrees and certificates in IU Online programs, with a focus on collaborative graduate programs.
- Explains curriculum requirements as well as school and campus policies.
- Meets with students 1-on-1 and/or in groups to consult on academic coursework that will meet their educational goals and the requirements of their selected degree program and/or certification.
- Refers students to appropriate campus resources, such as academic support resources, writing and math centers, career service opportunities, etc.
- Works with scheduling professionals to understand the capacities of each campus to support academic programs, recommend number of sections based on student demand, ensure courses reflect accurate prerequisite and requirement coding, and schedule students accordingly.
- Interfaces with program representative and/or faculty committees to discuss possible degree and/or certification requirement changes and share student feedback.
- Utilizes relationship management skills and the online collaborative model framework to navigate and work across university departments and campuses to provide timely (<24 business hours), accurate, and concise turn-around responses to student and faculty inquiries.
- Tracks and monitors students' academic progress. Reviews and maintains confidential student records to ensure that students meet requirements and to document advising discussions and communicates this information in a timely manner to students and to appropriate academic offices when necessary.
- Creates, updates, and disseminates advising materials, such as degree maps, FAQs, etc. Supports the transfer credit process and posting. Conducts graduate audits and degree conferrals.

General Responsibilities

- Provides academic counseling for students pursuing or considering majors, minors, or certificates. Guides students in planning their course of study in concert with the departments' curricular requirements. Explains curriculum requirements and school and campus policies.
- Meets with students in groups and 1-on-1 to guide students in academic programs that will meet their educational needs and the requirements of their chosen major, minor, and/or certificate.
- Assists students in making informed decisions about a choice of major and potential career or graduate school direction. Helps students to assess their interests, values, and academic skills and to understand these in relation to major choice and potential future career/graduate school options.
- Teaches students how to navigate university systems, academic processes, and policies. Empowers student accountability in academic decisions about courses, career direction, and long-term plans. Provides guidance on avenues for increased involvement as an IU student and in the IU community.
- Refers students to appropriate campus resources, such as academic support resources, placement programs, internship and overseas study opportunities, etc.
- Tracks and monitors students' academic progress, reviews and maintains confidential student records to ensure that students meet requirements and to document advising discussions, and communicates this information in a timely manner to students and to appropriate academic offices when necessary.
- Represents the advising function as a presenter at campus meetings and recruiting functions. Assists in developing written advising materials for use in student events.
- Researches, recommends, or creates best practices for unit or campus initiatives, projects, processes, or programs and may provide guidance to other Academic Advisors.

## Qualifications

_Combinations of related education and experience may be considered. Education beyond the minimum required may be substituted for work experience. Work experience beyond the minimum required may be substituted for education._

EDUCATION

**Required**

- Master's degree in related field.

WORK EXPERIENCE

**Required**

- 2 years in student affairs, teaching, academic advising, or related field. Experience in a student-focused, higher education environment.

**Preferred**

- 3 years in student affairs, teaching, academic advising, or related field. Experience in social, applied, and/or health-related disciplines.

SKILLS

**Required**

- Proficient written and verbal communication skills.
- Maintains a high degree of professionalism.
- Demonstrates time management and priority setting skills.
- Demonstrates a high commitment to quality.
- Possesses flexibility to work in a fast paced, dynamic environment.
- Seeks to acquire knowledge in area of specialty.
- Highly thorough and dependable.
- Demonstrates a high level of accuracy, even under pressure.
- Uses and learns new technology proficiently and changes practices with changing technology.
- Meet Best Practices and National Standards for Academic Advising.
- Understands and meets FERPA requirements.

## Working Conditions / Demands

This role requires the ability to effectively communicate and to operate a computer and other standard office productivity equipment. The position involves sedentary work as well as periods of time moving around an office environment and the campus. The person in this role must be able to perform the essential functions with or without an accommodation.

## Additional Information

Candidate proximity to south-central and central Indiana is desirable to attend in-person meetings and work events.

This position is part of the [IU Framework for Academic Advising and Career Development](https://go.iu.edu/aacd-framework). Learn more about the associated expectations, student learning outcomes, and institutional commitments at their website.

## Work Location

Bloomington, Indiana

This position is eligible for a hybrid schedule (mix between remote and in-person work), subject to change in the future based on university policy and business needs.

## Advertised Salary

Up to $54,169 per year

## Benefits Overview

For full-time staff employees, Indiana University offers a wide array of benefits including:

- Comprehensive medical and dental insurance
- Health savings account with generous IU contributions
- Healthcare and dependent care flexible spending accounts
- Basic group life insurance paid by IU
- Voluntary supplemental life, long-term disability, critical illness, and supplemental accidental death & dismemberment insurance
- Base retirement plan with generous IU contributions, subject to vesting
- Voluntary supplemental retirement plan options
- Tuition subsidy for employees and family members taking IU courses

- Employee assistance program (EAP)

Learn more about our benefits by reviewing the [IU Benefit Programs Brochure](https://hr.iu.edu/_docs/benefits-pubs/iu-benefits-brochure.pdf).

## Job Classification

Career Level: Career

FLSA: Exempt

Job Function: Student Services

Job Family: Academic Advising

[Click here to learn more about Indiana University's Job Framework.](https://hrms.iu.edu/psc/PH1PRD_PUB/EMPLOYEE/HRMS/c/IU_JC_COMPARE.IU_JC_COMPARE.GBL)

This posting is scheduled to close at 11:59 pm EST on the advertised Close Date. This posting may be closed at any time at the discretion of the University, but will remain open for a minimum of 5 business days. To guarantee full consideration, please submit your application within 5 business days of the Posted Date.

If you wish to include a cover letter, you may include it with your resume when uploading attachments.

## Equal Employment Opportunity

Indiana University is an equal opportunity employer and provider of ADA services and prohibits discrimination in hiring. [See Indiana University Notice of Non-Discrimination here which includes contact information](https://policies.iu.edu/policies/ua-01-non-discrimination/index.html).

The Annual Security and Fire Safety Report, containing policy statements, crime and fire statistics for all Indiana University campuses, is [available online](https://protect.iu.edu/iu-police-department/campus-security-reports/annual-security-reports/index.html). You may also request a physical copy by emailing IU Public Safety at [iups@iu.edu](mailto:iups@iu.edu) or by visiting IUPD.

title: Senior Workday Integration Developer
description:
Join our team! Our mission is BUILDING COMMUNITIES. IMPROVING LIVES. With a history spanning over 110 years, HR Green has consistently delivered on this mission, establishing alike. Each day, we work to find solutions that inspire our employees and fit our clients' needs to build trust to exceed their expectations. Our people are the heart of our success. We've earned national recognition, including being named a Great Place to Work and consistently ranking on Engineering News Record's Top 500 Design Firms in the United States and we're still growing!

Summary

HR Green is bringing its Workday integration portfolio in-house, and we are looking for a Senior Workday Integration Developer to own it. Our Workday environment connects HR, payroll, and finance data with key enterprise systems through custom Workday Studio integrations and packaged connectors. You will assume ownership of these integrations from our implementation partner, support them in production, adapt them as systems change, and build new integrations as our Workday capabilities expand.

This is a permanent, in-house, fully remote role within one of the states where we currently operate, including Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, South Dakota, Texas, not a project engagement. As the integration portfolio stabilizes, you will also become HR Green's technical resource for our firm-wide AI program: taking over AI agents and their supporting integrations built by external specialists, maintaining and adapting them, and building new ones, partnering with those specialists on larger implementations as the program grows. The AI work is applied development focused on secure, useful business solutions, not AI research or model development. If you are a Workday integration developer who wants to own an environment end to end, establish long-term internal ownership, and grow into applied AI work with real business impact, keep reading.

What You'll Do

  • Lead the transition of our Workday integrations from the implementation partner to internal ownership, including knowledge transfer, runbook and specification review, and setting up monitoring and support procedures
  • Serve as the primary support resource for production integrations, with priority on payroll-impacting feeds, and maintain the integration inventory and documentation
  • Design, build, test, and deploy new and modified integrations using Workday Studio, EIB, Core Connectors, Cloud Connect, Workday Web Services, Reports as a Service, and XSLT, including Studio integrations that call connected systems' REST APIs
  • Mature error handling, batch tracking, logging, and notifications so failures are caught before they affect payroll or onboarding
  • Plan and run integration regression testing for Workday releases and connected-system upgrades
  • Take over, maintain, and adapt AI agents and their supporting integrations, set the acceptance criteria that keep third-party deliverables maintainable, and build the secure API connectors and service identities that let approved agents work with HR Green systems
  • Build new agents and automations, independently or with external specialists, and apply our standards for agent testing, monitoring, and lifecycle management
  • Apply secure development practices and follow HR Green change-management, source-control, and release processes; some after-hours work is expected to support payroll-sensitive integrations
  • Perform other duties as assigned

What We're Looking for

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience
  • Five or more years developing and supporting system integrations, including three or more years building and supporting Workday integrations in production with hands-on Workday Studio development, and working familiarity with the broader Workday integration toolset (EIB, Core Connectors, Cloud Connect, Workday Web Services, Reports as a Service, XSLT)
  • Experience with taking ownership of integrations built by others and operated them reliably, including diagnosing failures across systems, root-cause analysis, and restoring service
  • Hands-on experience consuming REST and SOAP APIs, JSON and XML, and token-based and OAuth 2.0 authentication
  • Working proficiency in XML/XSLT and at least one general-purpose programming language, plus source control and code review
  • A candidate who can explain technical issues, risks, and trade-offs clearly to HR, Finance, and operations partners
  • Demonstrated aptitude and interest in applying AI and automation platforms to business problems
  • Experience building on LLM platforms or enterprise copilot/agent tooling is preferred
  • Experience integrating a professional-services ERP, payroll or benefits providers, identity directory, ITSM, or learning platforms is preferred
  • Proficiency in Python and working knowledge of SQL are preferred
  • Current or prior Workday integration certification or equivalent formal Workday Studio training, and cloud or AI certifications, are a plus

Why join HR Green?

  • It's your chance to join one of the country's longest-operating engineering firms and a leader in local markets in design engineering and construction with over 700 employees in 19 offices around the nation.
  • Not only does HR Green provide you with a place to grow, thrive, and enjoy your work, but we are also dedicated to delivering a comprehensive and multi-faceted benefits package.
  • Visit our website for detailed total rewards information.

Compensation Range

$114,000.00-171,700.00

The final agreed-upon compensation is based on a number of factors, including but not limited to: individual education, qualifications, skills, prior work experience, competencies, and geographic work location. The total annual compensation package may consist of a base salary and eligibility to participate, after a qualifying period, in our performance and discretionary incentive bonus program(s).

title: International Student Advisor
description:
- Location: Llandaff Campus
- Salary: £35,608 to £38,784 per annum
- Hours per week: 29.6
- Closing date: 11 November 2026

Working as part of the International Student Support Team within the Global Engagement Directorate, you will play a key role in ensuring international students receive an exceptional experience from arrival through to graduation. You will be responsible for coordinating welfare and support services, delivering immigration advice and leading activities that help students successfully settle into life at Cardiff Met. You will work with students from around the world, providing guidance on complex personal, practical and immigration matters, while helping to create an inclusive and welcoming international community.

This is a varied and rewarding role that combines student support, project management, immigration advice and team leadership. You'll use your expertise, cultural awareness and problem-solving skills to make a meaningful difference to students' lives and contribute to Cardiff Met's global ambitions.

You’ll lead the way by:

- Demonstrating detailed knowledge and understanding of the UK government’s immigration regulations, ensuring accurate advice is provided to students about their immigration status via 1-1 visa extension appointments; group workshops and the issuing of Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS).
- Project managing the arrival and welcome of new international students. Using initiative and forward thinking to develop systems to respond to the challenging and fast-changing environment and needs of international students.
- Overseeing and co-ordinating the service provision offered at the Global Lounge, with line management responsibility for Assistant International Student Advisors.
- Using high level problem solving skills and cultural awareness to support international students experiencing complex personal problems or emergency situations, advocating for students and supporting them with sensitivity and professionalism.
- Responsibility for project managing social events including the annual Global Week events, by devising and planning the programme of events, engaging with the local community, student body and staff to encourage participation and broadly promoting the benefits of cultural awareness, inclusivity and acceptance.
- Representing the interests of the Global Engagement Directorate and Cardiff Met international students in internal and external networks, events, meetings, working groups and steering groups.

**What you’ll bring**

With experience of supporting students in a higher education setting, you'll be passionate about delivering an outstanding student experience and helping students from diverse cultural backgrounds to thrive. Your knowledge of international student issues, combined with your ability to interpret and apply immigration regulations, will enable you to provide accurate, timely and compassionate advice on a wide range of personal, welfare and visa-related matters.

An excellent communicator with strong organisational skills, you'll be confident managing a varied workload, building effective relationships with stakeholders, and coordinating activities that enhance the international student experience. You'll use sound judgement, initiative and cultural awareness to resolve complex situations and contribute to a welcoming, inclusive and supportive community.

Additionally, you'll:

- Have experience of providing advice, guidance and support to students, including the ability to deal sensitively and effectively with complex or challenging cases.
- Possess knowledge of UK Student visa regulations and the wider issues affecting international students studying in higher education.
- Be able to communicate complex information clearly and effectively, both verbally and in writing, to a diverse range of audiences.
- Demonstrate strong organisational and administrative skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines in a busy environment.
- Have experience of planning and coordinating projects, events or activities, ensuring successful delivery and positive outcomes.
- Build productive working relationships with colleagues, external organisations and stakeholders to enhance the support available to students.
- Be confident using a range of IT systems and digital tools to deliver services, maintain records and produce reports.
- Have experience of line management or staff supervision, together with a willingness to work occasional weekends and unsociable hours during peak operational periods when required.
- Hold a degree or possess equivalent relevant professional experience.

**Why join Cardiff Metropolitan University?**

We are a values-based University. We are proud of our culture, and we are there for our people. Our community spirit is the golden thread that underpins our values and behaviours. We support and embrace inclusion that enables everyone to feel respected and able to perform at their best. By joining our University, you'll find yourself in a unique environment where a wealth of knowledge and resources are readily available, supporting you with your career development.

We offer excellent benefits such as:

- Annual leave of 25 days, rising to 30 days after 1 years’ service, plus 12 bank holiday / concessionary days.
- Membership of the Local Government Pension Scheme with generous monthly contributions.
- Excellent family friendly policies – take a look on our Policy Hub page.
- Opportunities to learn and develop your skills with access to library and digital services facilities.
- Excellent sports and fitness facilities with subsidised membership.
- Free family access to our independent specialist wellbeing support provider, Health Assured.

**Contact us**

All applications must be submitted online.

The person specification will be used as a tool for shortlisting; so please make sure you use this information when writing your application. You can find useful hints and tips about how to apply by visiting our [Application Guidance page.](https://recruitment.cardiffmet.ac.uk/application-support/)

title: Permanent Supportive Housing Manager
description:
Job Title

Permanent Supportive Housing Manager

Reports to:

Director of Permanent Supportive Housing & Property Development

FLSA / Wage

Non-Exempt/$14.42 per hour for 20 hours per week. Also free employer- housing provided.

Orig. Date

January 2016

Revised:

May 2024


JOB SUMMARY

To manage the Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH) program and lead the supportive services team.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  1. Value cultural competence and diversity
    1. Collaborate with staff, members, and the community to gain the perspectives of others having diverse opinions, abilities, values, beliefs, perspective, and ethnic or cultural backgrounds.
    2. Take deliberate steps to increase their own cultural competency by attending trainings, events, discussions, workshops, etc.
  2. Facilitates a smooth move-in process for new residents.
    1. Receives referrals and conducts interviews for potential residents. Provides choices to applicants by showing available properties. Facilitates lease signing and all related intake paperwork.
    2. Educates residents on housing procedures including paying rent and reporting maintenance problems.
    3. Maintains a waiting list and ensures vacancies are filled within the timeframes required by funders.


  1. Ensures services are delivered by the PSH team with a recovery-oriented, trauma-informed approach.
    1. Provides day-to-day supervision of PSH Coordinators to achieve program goals of housing stability, community integration, and increased resources and support.
    2. Provides ongoing training to PSH Coordinators on the principles of Housing First, Recovery Principles, Psychiatric Rehabilitation, Motivational Interviewing, and Trauma-informed Care.
    3. Ensures that development and implementation of Recovery Plans is consistent with organizational values, program goals, and evidence-based practices.
    4. Guides staff in providing case management utilizing trauma-informed care, harm reduction, assertive engagement, and a strengths-based approach, in alignment with PSH best practices.
    5. Inspires staff to empower the residents and encourage autonomy and a sense of self-determination.
    6. Oversees coordination of services with internal and external providers
    7. Supports staff in handling difficult or complex cases.


  1. Ensures accreditation and funding source requirements are met.
    1. Ensures timely and accurate documentation is completed by the PSH Coordinators (progress notes, recovery plans, DLA-20s, etc.)
    2. Ensures residents are seen at least two times a month in accordance with TDMHSAS requirements.
  2. Administrative Responsibilities:
    1. Coordinates with Property Manager on all property management functions (e.g., leasing, orientation, inspections, maintenance requests, evictions, etc.)
    2. Ensures each resident has an electronic client file containing referral information, up-to-date leases, progress notes, financial verification if required, and other pertinent documentation.
    3. Assists Director in maintaining and reporting monthly housing data and outcomes.
    4. Assists Director in developing and revising policies and procedures.
    5. Complies with TDMHSAS grant requirements for Community Supportive Housing.


  1. Supervisory Responsibilities:
    1. Orients new staff to program mission, goals, policies, and procedures.
    2. Oversees job responsibilities of the Lead PSH Coordinator, Peer PSH Coordinator(s) and PSH Coordinator(s) and other personnel related to the PSH program.
    3. Conducts and documents weekly supervision, quarterly work plans, monthly audits on progress notes and service plans and performance reviews of supervised staff.


  1. Public/Staff Relations:
    1. Develops positive working relationships with landlords, neighbors, and community agencies.
    2. Works with MDHA and other agencies, committees and organizations as assigned on housing issues.
    3. Utilizes voice and email.
    4. Communicates regularly with other staff to meet the needs of members and residents.
    5. Works as a team player with other staff.


  1. Values cultural competence and diversity:
    1. Collaborates with staff, members, and the community to gain the perspectives of others having diverse opinions, abilities, values, beliefs, perspectives, and ethnic or cultural backgrounds.
    2. Take deliberate steps to increase own cultural competency by attending trainings, events, discussions, workshops, etc.
    3. Is intentional to increase cultural competency within the department.


  1. Other duties as a Member of Park Center Permanent Supportive Housing team:
    1. Leads staff and supervision meetings.
    2. Assists with housing events.
    3. Participates in on-call rotation.
    4. Maintains good attendance and informs supervisor in advance of annual leave or other time off.
    5. Follows all Personnel Policies.
    6. Completes required Relias Learning yearly.
    7. Other duties as assigned.


QUALIFICATIONS


  • Ability to work independently and with a team.
  • Ability to meet deadlines.
  • Excellent communication skills.
  • Strong professional and ethical behaviors.
  • Must have bachelor’s degree in a human services field.
  • Must have at least 3 years’ experience working in a human services field.
  • At least 1 year of experience in a supervisory role preferred.
  • Must be a CPRP or be willing to be certified.
  • Must have a valid Tennessee Driver’s License.


WORKING CONDITIONS


  • Will have a desk, workstation and an office.
  • Able to operate with many distractions.
  • Routine office environment
  • Able to use vehicle to transport clients.


PHYSICAL DEMANDS


  • The ability to communicate effectively in written and oral form.
  • The ability to navigate stairs and uneven terrain.
  • The ability to operate with many distractions.
  • The ability to use vehicle to travel to different sites.


The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by any employee to perform the essential functions of their job at Park Center. Reasonable accommodations, physical or otherwise, may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

DIRECT REPORTS

(3) Recovery Support Coordinator II

(3) Peer Recovery Support Coordinator II

(1) Licensed Alcohol and Drug Abuse Counselor

(1) Apartment Monitor


SCHEDULE



WORK LOCATION

  • Hybrid: field work in Nashville, TN, shared office space, remote office capability


DISCLAIMER


This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive, and the employee will be expected to perform other reasonably related duties as assigned. Park Center reserves the right to revise or change job tasks and responsibilities.

title: Program Specialist - Ruma
description:
Position Summary:

Program Specialists (Rental Processors) are responsible for providing direct services to clients through intake, documentation collection, eligibility determination, and case follow-up. This role is foundational to program success and client outcomes.

Key Responsibilities:

Compliance and Training

• Ensure accountability by maintaining departmental metrics, Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), and adhering to contract compliance standards

• Attend all training as necessary

Application Assistance

• Provide clear and empathetic communication with clients, ensuring complete applications and submission of all necessary documentation.

• Maintain weekly spend rate amounts for each RUMA program for timely contract execution and delivery ( subject to change depending on department needs)

• Communicate with landlords to explain the rental assistance program, document collection, verify payment acceptance, and confirm payee information.

• Process check requests for rental, utility and rebate assistance.

• Full understanding of lease agreements and ledgers.

• Maintain a thorough understanding of tenant/landlord rights and the eviction processes.

• Maintain comprehensive and accurate case notes in the agency database and web-based applications throughout the client service period.

• Manage a high-volume email account, responding promptly to client inquiries.

• Maintain organized electronic files and efficiently process case reviews and approvals.

• Refer clients to budget/credit workshops, which will provide an educational service to increase financial literacy, as needed or requested.

Qualifications

• Experience in housing case management, human services, or a related field, preferably working with low-income households or vulnerable populations.

• Strong understanding of rental assistance processes, lease agreements, ledgers, and tenant/landlord rights.

• Familiarity with eviction prevention strategies and community-based housing resources.

• Demonstrated ability to manage sensitive client information with professionalism, empathy, and confidentiality.

• Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage high volumes of email correspondence, documentation, and electronic file systems.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex processes clearly to clients and landlords.

• Proficiency with web-based applications and case management databases; ability to maintain accurate, timely, and complete records.

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, compliance-driven environment.

• Bilingual skills (English/Spanish) strongly preferred.

• High school diploma or equivalent required; associate or bachelor’s degree in human services, social work, or a related field preferred.

LOCATION:

This is a hybrid position with one day in office at BRI’s Edgewater location. Subject to change as needed for RUMA department and BRI.

MENTAL DEMANDS:

PHYSICAL DEMAND CLASSIFICATION: LIGHT (Occasionally lifts up to 25 pounds)

PHYSICAL AND COMMUNICATION DEMANDS:

• Constant (67-100%): Forward reaching, grasping, handling, fingering, vision, hearing, sight with color perception, writing or composing in the English language, reading.

• Frequent (34-66%): Sitting, talking to coworkers, talking on the phone, responding to written/verbal requests from coworkers, responding to written/verbal requests, receiving verbal instructions, receiving written instructions.

• Occasional (1-33%): Standing, walking, stair climbing, bending, squatting, kneeling, stooping, crouching, climbing, twisting, side bending, over-head reach, talking to customers, written communication to customers.

DESCRIPTION OF TASKS:

• Pushing/Pulling: Occasional pushing/pulling is required when the employee is using hand truck to move files or office supplies. Force pounds were estimated to be up to 25#.

• Lifting/Carrying: Occasional lifting/carrying is required when the employee is moving files, boxes, and office supplies. Force pounds were estimated to be up to 25#.

• Sitting: The employee sits constantly at a work station or desk.

• Standing/Walking: Alternate standing and walking is performed occasionally when employee is walking to make copies at the copying machine, faxing documents, or going to assist others in the company.

• Climbing: Climbing is performed when the employee needs to climb onto a step stool to reach items on shelves.

• Bending/Stooping/Crouching: Forward torso bending, stooping, and crouching may be preference of the worker when reaching or material handling at lowered work surfaces, and/or reaching for items on the lower shelves.

• Squatting/Kneeling: These techniques can be used by the employee when performing lifting, carrying, or with position tolerance tasks. Squatting/kneeling can be applied up to 1/3 of the workday.

This position has regular verbal and written contact with administrative personnel, middle, and senior management. The nature of these communications range from a routine exchange of information to a process of securing information and/or responding to inquiries where explanation and discussion may be required using judgment.

EQUIPMENT, MACHINES, TOOLS USED:

Computer, computer software, scanner, printer, telephone, copier, facsimile machine, calculator, postage machine, paper cutter, and hand truck. May use other equipment as required for the position.

DESCRIPTION OF WORK ENVIRONMENT:

Environmental Exposure:

Inside: 100% Temperature: Air-conditioned room

Work is performed primarily indoors unless the employee is required to go out of the office on errands. Employee will be in contact with chemicals (i.e., toner for copier and facsimile machines), and materials (i.e., paper) normally found at offices. Employee will also be exposed to minimal noise and vibration.

Vision and Hearing:

Must be able to clearly see the computer monitor with or without corrected vision. Must be able to judge or distinguish distance and space relationships.

Must be able to hear within a normal range with or without a hearing device.

BENEFITS:

403B with 3% match, Health Insurance, Dental Insurance, Vision Insurance, Life Insurance, Paid time off including vacation, sick and personal leave; plus, paid holidays; and a solid working environment!
